prompt: Use case: scientific-educational. Create one friendly abstract clearly drawn comic-style chemistry learning-goal illustration, PNG, landscape approximately 16:9 around 1600 by 900 pixels. A clear large acid-base titration apparatus occupies most of the picture, usable at 360px phone width and 680px desktop width. White warm background, soft teal and coral accents, bold rounded outlines, no photorealism, no sterile technical blueprint. Show a securely clamped vertical burette filled with dilute sodium hydroxide standard solution above a wide-base Erlenmeyer flask containing a measured hydrochloric acid sample and indicator on a white tile. Burette must have a recognisable stopcock and a narrow delivery tip pointing down into the flask mouth, with a single droplet; the liquid falls into the flask, not onto the bench. The solution in the flask is pale pink only at the illustrated phenolphthalein endpoint, not intensely coloured; a gentle swirl arrow around the flask means mixing. Burette graduations increase downwards, only two legible numbers '0' near the top and '25' farther down, simple evenly spaced ticks, no false measured result or concentration. Use only these few large accurate annotations: 'Maßlösung NaOH', 'Probe HCl', 'Indikator', and 'Volumen ablesen'. Include a small closed indicator bottle and a simple blank measurement notebook at the base; no written answers, numerical concentration, result or equations. If any notebook markings are shown they must be oriented correctly for a person standing at the bench facing the apparatus, not upside-down for that person. No visible person or hand is needed. Clear coherent apparatus, no impossible glassware, no funnel left in the burette during titration, no disconnected liquid tube, no electric wiring, no decorative clutter, no branding or technical IDs. This illustrates a planned documented titration workflow, without substituting for the learner's reasoning or experimental performance.
